answer.reason: When max_attempts is None, routes[:None] copies the whole list, which matches skipping the slice. For any other value, both versions run the same slice, so no input tells them apart and the cap still works.
sources: A request shall never attempt more routes than the configured route-attempt limit.

review.reason: In Python, slicing a list with None as the stop index (`routes[:None]`) returns a full copy containing all elements, which produces the exact same tuple as skipping the slice when options.max_attempts is None. For all other values, both versions perform the exact same slicing, so no input can distinguish between them.
